name: Jeffrey Epstein
current_role: Financier and convicted sex offender (died August 10, 2019)
summary: Jeffrey Epstein was a New York financier who managed money for wealthy clients, chiefly retail billionaire Les Wexner, and cultivated ties with prominent figures in politics, business and academia. He pleaded guilty in Florida in 2008 to state charges including soliciting a minor for prostitution, was arrested on federal sex-trafficking charges in July 2019, and died in a Manhattan jail on August 10, 2019, in a death ruled a suicide. Congress ordered the release of the government’s Epstein files in November 2025, and the Justice Department published about 3.5 million pages in January 2026.

connections.name: Donald Trump
connections.description: Trump and Epstein socialized from the late 1980s into the early 2000s; in a 2002 New York magazine profile Trump said he had known Epstein for 15 years and called him a “terrific guy,” and flight logs entered at Ghislaine Maxwell’s 2021 trial show Trump on Epstein’s plane several times between 1993 and 1997. Public sightings ended around 2004, when they bid against each other for a Palm Beach mansion; Trump has said they had a falling out, that he threw Epstein out of Mar-a-Lago and “wasn’t a fan.” In July 2025 Trump sued the Wall Street Journal over its report of a 2003 birthday letter it attributed to him, which he denies writing.
